question: Where do lung cancer cells most commonly start growing?

options.A: Alveolar macrophages in the lung parenchyma
options.B: Smooth muscle layers of the bronchioles
options.D: Epithelial lining of the respiratory tract

explanation: Lung cancers typically start in the epithelial cells that line the airways and tiny air sacs of the respiratory system. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why do many patients with lung cancer arrive at clinics in the late stages of the disease?

options.A: Patients have natural immunity against early tumors
options.B: Malignant cells multiply faster in tropical climates
options.C: Symptoms often look like common long-term chest infections
options.D: Primary healthcare workers refuse to perform chest X-rays

explanation: Early signs like a lingering cough are often mistaken for tuberculosis or bronchitis, which delays proper testing. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is known as the leading cause of lung cancer around the world?
explanation: Tobacco smoke contains harmful chemicals that directly damage the DNA inside respiratory cells. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: A patient who cooks with firewood every day in a poorly ventilated kitchen is at risk for lung cancer mainly because of what factor?

options.A: Indoor air pollution from biomass smoke
options.B: Direct thermal injury to the alveoli

explanation: Breathing in smoke from solid fuels causes ongoing inflammation and cellular damage, similar to cigarette smoke. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is the main difference between Small Cell Lung Cancer and Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?

options.A: Rapid cellular growth and early spreading
options.C: Origin in the pleural lining exclusively
options.D: Resistance to all forms of chemotherapy

explanation: Small cell lung cancer multiplies quickly and spreads to other parts of the body early on. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of these is a type of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?
explanation: Adenocarcinoma is a common type of non-small cell lung cancer that usually starts in the outer areas of the lung tissue. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: What symptom is often the first sign that a lung tumor is eroding into the airway lining?
explanation: Coughing up blood happens when a growing tumor damages blood vessels in the airway lining. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why do many patients with lung cancer experience sudden weight loss and constant tiredness?

options.A: Severe allergic reactions to air pollutants
options.B: Metabolic changes and body-wide effects caused by the tumor
options.C: Complete physical inability to chew or swallow food
options.D: Excessive fluid retention replacing body fat

explanation: Tumors can release substances that change how the body uses energy, leading to a wasting condition called cachexia. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using the TNM staging system for lung cancer?

options.A: Calculating the patient's daily caloric requirement
options.B: Checking tumor size, lymph node involvement, and spreading
options.C: Determining the exact bacterial load in the bronchi
options.D: Measuring the patient's baseline respiratory rate

explanation: The TNM system helps doctors classify how far the cancer has spread based on the main tumor, nearby lymph nodes, and distant sites. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why is a tissue biopsy needed after a doctor spots a suspicious shadow on a chest X-ray?

options.A: To prevent the development of secondary bacterial infections
options.B: To confirm the specific type of cancer cells present
options.C: To clear blocked airways of thick mucus secretions
options.D: To reduce the overall size of the primary tumor mass

explanation: X-rays only suggest a problem, but looking at a tissue sample under a microscope is required to prove it is cancer and find the exact cell type. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h5)

question: Which treatment offers the best chance for a cure in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer?
explanation: Cutting out the cancerous tissue gives the highest chance of long-term survival when the tumor is still in one place. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why are chemotherapy and radiation used instead of surgery for small cell lung cancer?

options.A: The cancer usually spreads widely before it is detected
options.B: Patients with this cancer never have underlying heart disease
options.C: Small cell tumors grow too slowly to be targeted by surgery
options.D: Surgical instruments cannot reach the lower lobes of the lungs

explanation: Because small cell lung cancer spreads very early, body-wide medications and radiation are needed to treat microscopic disease all over. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is a key nursing action to help a patient manage thick mucus in their airways?

options.C: Encouraging the patient to drink enough fluids

explanation: Drinking plenty of fluids helps thin out respiratory mucus so the patient can cough it up more easily. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)

question: How should a nurse manage pain for a patient with advanced lung cancer affecting the chest wall?

options.A: Give pain medicine only when the patient cries out
options.B: Follow the WHO pain ladder with scheduled pain medications
options.C: Rely solely on relaxation techniques without pharmaceutical agents
options.D: Avoid opioids to prevent any possibility of breathing changes

explanation: Using a structured medication schedule helps provide steady and reliable relief for cancer pain. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the main focus of community health nursing when it comes to preventing lung cancer?

options.A: Performing routine cancer surgeries in local clinics
options.B: Isolating individuals with long-term chest infections
options.C: Promoting stopping tobacco use and reducing environmental risks
options.D: Giving preventive chemotherapy to healthy adults

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on stopping people from being exposed to known causes of cancer, like tobacco and indoor smoke. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why is teaching the community about persistent coughs so important in primary healthcare?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never develop lung cancer
options.B: It encourages people to report symptoms early and get checked
options.C: It proves that all long-term coughs are just simple allergies
options.D: It eliminates the need for expensive lab tests

explanation: Teaching the public to seek help early for unresolved symptoms helps catch cancer before it becomes advanced. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h8)
